title: Immigration Hardliner Stephen Miller Named Trump's New White House Chief of Staff
snippet: President Trump has appointed longtime adviser Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff following GOP midterm losses, placing the controversial architect of the administration's aggressive enforcement agenda at the helm of the West Wing.
content:
President Donald Trump has appointed top senior adviser Stephen Miller as his next White House chief of staff, elevating the central architect of his administration's hardline immigration policies to the highest staff position in the executive branch. Miller, who officially assumes the role on Monday, replaces Susie Wiles, who served as chief of staff through the start of Trump's second term.

A Pivotal Post-Midterm Realignment

Trump announced the major staffing change on Friday, calling Miller one of his 'most trusted' advisers. The shake-up follows significant Republican losses in the midterm elections and arrives as congressional Democrats ready broad investigations into the White House's executive actions and border policies.

Rather than pulling back under congressional scrutiny, Miller's promotion signals an unwavering commitment to the administration's signature agenda. Miller has been key in leveraging the $170 billion for immigration enforcement and border security passed under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in July 2025.

Supercharging Deportation Targets and Novel Legal Strategies

During Trump's second term, Miller pushed Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to hit an aggressive target of at least 3,000 arrests per day. That effort expanded federal detentions deep into local communities, workplaces, and courts, significantly raising the number of non-criminal immigrants swept into custody and fueling protests nationwide.

Miller also pushed the boundaries of executive authority by advocating for National Guard deployments to assist in mass deportations and invoking the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 to rapidly deport alleged Venezuelan gang members to El Salvador. That strategy sparked intense legal resistance, culminating in a Supreme Court stay preventing immediate deportations without due process. In addition, Miller floated the idea of suspending habeas corpus for immigration detainees and suggested using military force against international drug cartels.

A Legacy of Controversial Policies

Miller’s influence has shaped the Trump doctrine since the president's first administration. He was instrumental in designing the original 2017 travel restriction on several Muslim-majority countries, the 2018 'zero-tolerance' family separation policy, and historic reductions in U.S. refugee caps.

More recently, Miller stood alongside President Trump in the Oval Office to champion new executive actions aimed at restricting birthright citizenship following Supreme Court pushback. Now, as chief of staff, Miller will oversee the entire White House operation as it prepares to face an empowered opposition in Congress.
